title: Toot, Whistle, Plunk and Boom (1953) — musicians
creator: Walt Disney Productions; directed by Charles Nichols and Ward Kimball
credit: Toot, Whistle, Plunk and Boom (1953) · Disney / D23
rationale: An unmistakable midcentury modernist animation scene: elongated angular musicians, delicate economical lines, flat pink/purple shapes and playful abstract instruments. D23 explicitly describes this Disney film as using the UPA style; it is not itself a UPA production.
quality_targets: Playful exaggerated silhouettes built from long angular limbs and bold flat head and costume shapes.
Economical fine contour and decorative lines over a restrained, harmonious pink-purple palette.
Characters, instruments and scenery share stylized geometry and deliberate negative space.
use: Internal visual reference, not a production asset or an ownership/license claim

title: RSA Animate: Changing Education Paradigms
creator: Royal Society of Arts / Cognitive
credit: RSA Animate · Royal Society of Arts / Cognitive
rationale: The official RSA upload uses confident marker drawings, small expressive people, handwritten explanations and one accent color. Text is part of this visual treatment, not thumbnail decoration to reproduce.
quality_targets: Confident dark contour lines on a clean white field, with readable small faces and hands.
One restrained accent color that groups ideas and directs attention.
Characters, diagrams and short labels arranged with clear spacing and an obvious reading order.
use: Internal visual reference, not a production asset or an ownership/license claim

title: We’re Going on a Bear Hunt — ident artwork
creator: Lupus Films
credit: We’re Going on a Bear Hunt · Lupus Films
rationale: This studio artwork puts expressive drawn people into a complete, textured landscape. It shows the intended finish at scene scale, including atmosphere and staging, rather than only a textured character.
quality_targets: Visible pencil and watercolor-like grain that remains consistent across figures and scenery.
Soft, harmonious color and value separation between the figures, foreground and distant landscape.
Readable running poses and integrated ground contact inside a complete illustrated composition.
use: Internal visual reference, not a production asset or an ownership/license claim

title: Charlie and Lola — leaf costume and drawn character designs
creator: Lauren Child / Charlie and Lola production
credit: Lauren Child / Milkmonitor Ltd. · Charlie and Lola
rationale: A photographic leaf becomes a costume around an economical drawn face and limbs. This makes mixed-media collage unmistakable while preserving a coherent character and continuous limb connections.
quality_targets: Photographic texture confined to a clear, deliberately cut silhouette.
Hand-drawn faces, hair and limbs that retain one consistent visual scale.
Clean overlaps and readable limb exits where the textured costume meets drawn body parts.
use: Internal visual reference, not a production asset or an ownership/license claim

title: Simpsons Pixels
creator: Ivan Dixon and Paul Robertson
credit: Simpsons Pixels · Ivan Dixon and Paul Robertson
rationale: The creators’ pixel animation uses deliberate block shapes, a limited palette and clear silhouettes, with a fully designed living-room environment. This is pixel design, not simply a blur or mosaic filter.
quality_targets: Consistent, crisp square pixel edges with no smeared or antialiased contours.
Recognizable character silhouettes and faces using economical clusters of color.
Environment, props and figures share the same pixel scale and palette discipline.
use: Internal visual reference, not a production asset or an ownership/license claim

title: Sigma Origin Story — illustrated key image
creator: Blizzard Entertainment / Overwatch origin-story team
rationale: A polished cinematic illustrated frame with a strong central figure, readable hands, controlled light and layered debris. It represents illustrated-film / motion-comic presentation, not proof that our rig reproduces its full anatomy or animation.
quality_targets: One strong focal pose with readable face and hands against a controlled background.
Deliberate shape-based shadows and highlights that support volume without muddying the silhouette.
Foreground and background elements composed to create depth while keeping the story action clear.
use: Internal visual reference, not a production asset or an ownership/license claim

title: Yuki 7 — Hong Kong style frame
creator: Elaine Lee / Chromosphere
credit: Hong Kong style frame: Elaine Lee · Yuki 7 / Chromosphere
rationale: A rich graphic scene with clear foreground vehicles, midground people and architecture, and receding streets. The still is a quality reference for layered staging; it cannot by itself demonstrate parallax, and the source production uses a more extensive 2D/3D hybrid pipeline.
quality_targets: Clearly separated foreground, action plane and distant environment through scale, overlap and value.
A controlled luminous palette that makes the intended focal area stand out.
Environment detail and small figures designed in one coherent graphic style.
use: Internal visual reference, not a production asset or an ownership/license claim
